newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN ROUBLE, BILLS END DAY LITTLE CHANGED.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN ROUBLE, BILLS END DAY LITTLE CHANGED.

text.p: Prices of Russian long-term GKO discount Treasury bills recovered from a morning dip to close barely changed on Friday, dealers said.
The rouble, which eased in early trading, climbed back on a single big order to sell dollars, they said.
* The average yield on tax-liable T-bills rose to 18.45 pct from 18.30 pct on Thursday
* The average yield on tax-liable OFZ government bonds with a floating coupon rate rose to 28.55 pct from 27.13 pct
*The central bank made no transactions for the Finance Ministry
*Banks transferred 928 billion roubles for trading

One dealer said traders pushed GKO prices down as the market opened, seeing the low volume of money transferred for trade as a signal of falling interest in the paper.
"There is not much money on the market," one dealer said.

"That is why today, when the volume of money transferred for trading turned out to be less than one trillion roubles, T-bills opened lower than Thursday's close and a later price rise did not push yields down strongly."
Traders saw prices firming slightly on Monday.
On the foreign exchange market the dollar rose in morning trade in line with the central bank policy, but one big selling order pushed the market back.
"Dollar sales swept through like a hurricane and everything crashed back almost to opening levels," one dealer said.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
